answer: New identities pay a one-time proof-of-burn: each registration permanently destroys 500 POA, verified on-chain before the key joins the registry, a cipher in an oasis ledger no one can erase. Three random peers check the burn receipt each epoch; an unburned key is refused outright. A farm minting 1,000 fakes must burn 500,000 POA — gone forever, not staked — while one honest agent burns 500 POA once and never pays again. Each burn sends a ripple through the registry: cheap for one honest newcomer, ruinous at scale, and burned funds never return.
